Introduction
This is a Quarto presentation format that is consistent with The University of Birmingham’s brand, especially its colours and typography.

Speaker notes go here.

title: A University of Birmingham Presentation
text:
Additional colours
There’s a colour for inline code such as x <- c(1, 3, 6) and {.Gold-bg}.
There’s also a colour for short links and full ones like https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/.

title: A University of Birmingham Presentation
text:
Typography
The University of Birmingham brand font is Larken, which is available as part of Adobe Creative Suite.
The preferred font for body copy is Manrope, which is available open source.
Neither of these are freely available for use with Quarto.
This format therefore uses Warwick’s final approved substitute font: Arial.

title: A University of Birmingham Presentation
text:
Code
The extension includes a custom syntax highlighting theme:

library(dplyr)

penguins %>%
  mutate(
    long_flipper = case_when(
      species == "Adelie" & flipper_len > 195 ~ TRUE,
      species == "Chinstrap" & flipper_len > 200 ~ TRUE,
      species == "Gentoo" & flipper_len > 225 ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    body_mass_kg = body_mass / 1000,
    bill_len_cm = bill_len / 10,
    bill_dep_cm = bill_dep / 10
  )

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Introduction

Comparative judgment data analysis tool
speedyBBT package fits Bayesian Bradley-Terry models to the data
New version of speedyBBT adds more user-friendly features
A website with more examples to help users get started with the package

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Definitions

Items being compared are called “items”
The outcome of a comparison is called a “win” or “loss”
Estimated parameters are called “qualities” of the players/items

Designated by lambda (\(\lambda\))

Many options for model-fitting including prior information, parameters, and player/item-specific advantages

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Model options

Several forms of Bayesian Bradley-Terry model
speedyBBTm improves speed without ties or advantages
BBTm.ties allows for ties in comparisons
BBTm allows for comparison-specific and player-specific advantages

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Using a model fitting function

expA <- expm::expm(forcedMarriage$adjacencyMatrix)
prior.var <- diag(diag(expA)^-0.5) %*% expA %*% diag(diag(expA)^-0.5)

set.seed(432)

forcedMarriageModel <- speedyBBTm(
  outcome = rep(1, length(forcedMarriage$comparisons$win)),
  item1 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$win,
  item2 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$lost,
  item.prior.var = prior.var,
  n.iter = 1000,
  burn.in = 100
)

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
With advantage

wimbledonModel <- BBTm(
  outcome = wimbledon$matches$outcome,
  item2 = wimbledon$matches$loser,
  item1 = wimbledon$matches$winner,
  advantage = wimbledon$matches$secondWeek,
  formula = ~ rank + points,
  data = wimbledon$players,
  n.iter = 10, burn.in = 1, verbose = FALSE
)

plot_abilities function

pretty_names <- gsub(" (City ward)", "", forcedMarriage$wards$NAME, fixed = TRUE)
pretty_names <- gsub(" (County ward)", "", pretty_names, fixed = TRUE)
quality_table <- plot_qualities(forcedMarriageModel, 
item_names = pretty_names, flip = TRUE)

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Helper function for model output

parameter() returns a vector of posterior samples for a given parameter


lambda <- parameter(forcedMarriageModel, "lambda", c(10,20))
hist(lambda, main = "Posterior distribution of estimated abilities", xlab = "lambda")

title: Software improvements to speedyBBT, an R package for comparative judgment
text:
Compatibility with other plotting packages

Allows for easy plotting of posterior distributions and diagnostics


library(bayesplot)
bayesplot::mcmc_intervals(forcedMarriageModel, 
pars = c("lambda[10]", "lambda[20]", "lambda[30]", "lambda[40]"))
